svg.title: Answering input_required: no callback, the driven loop, and the hand-driven loop
svg.desc: A band at the top states that passing an elicitation callback is what puts the elicitation capability into the client capabilities carried in the meta block of every request, and that the manual path never invokes the callback and still needs one. Below it are three lanes of equal width. The first connects without a callback and dead-ends: the server refuses with error minus thirty-two thousand and twenty-one, missing required client capability, before it ever asks, the payload names the capability that was missing, and a cross marks that there is no result, no question and nothing to retry. The second passes a callback and lets the software development kit drive: the server returns a result whose type is input_required, the kit calls the callback once per entry of the input requests map, and it retries with the same tool name, the same arguments, a new identifier and the request state echoed verbatim, with a note that you write none of it. The third passes a callback and drives the same loop by hand through call_tool with allow input required set true, answering every key the server chose and calling again with the same name, arguments and echoed request state, with a note that this is what a host batching two servers into one dialog needs. The second and third lanes converge on a band saying both hand back the same CallToolResult. A closing band explains the round cap: the loop is bounded at ten rounds by default and then raises, and it is reached when a server rewords its question between rounds, because the recorded answer is matched against a digest of the exact text.
svg.text: Two ways to answer, and one thing that is not optional
A server cannot ask. It returns, and waits to be called again. What differs is who drives the second call.
Passing a callback is what declares the capability
It goes into clientCapabilities in the _meta of every request. The manual path never invokes it, and still needs one.
